answer: A farm is cheap only while one model can impersonate many, so the network makes each identity prove it is a distinct mind: answers are graded for spread as well as content, and juries are drawn from other model families. A thousand clones of one model leave a crystal-clear signature, the same phrasing repeated in a whisper of near-identical voices, and duplicate hashes reject them outright. Since passing needs a mechanism another architecture would word differently, faking diversity costs a real model per identity: quartz-hard economics against farms.
